title: I Spent Two Years Building the Median — Hariprasad Sudharshan
talk_summary: A product manager argues that AI coding agents converge on the same 'median' solution for any given problem, so building the median is free and non-differentiating; the scarce resource is novelty and human judgment. He offers a few process heuristics (search before building, name the novelty, treat 'AI says done' as the start of work) rather than any technical mechanism.

takeaways.evidence_quote: Why did you build the nth rag system when more mature, feature-rich, open-source systems are available with thousands of stars and maturity?

takeaways.technique: Treat 'agent says done' as the start of review, not the end
takeaways.what_they_do: Interpret an agent's completion signal as 'median output delivered' and schedule human/stronger-model work after it, rather than accepting the first green result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When AI says done, then it means that to me, okay, AI has given its median product. I have to start working from here.

takeaways.technique: Don't roadmap on small frontier gaps; compare harnesses not models
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues leaderboard Elo deltas are relative and small, and that most 'model comparisons' are actually harness comparisons (tools, context, orchestration), so differentiation should come from the harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We mistakenly compare the harness or the product for models. The Claude code versus Cursor or Codex isn't a model comparison.
takeaways.numbers: Anthropic 1503 vs Mistral 1460 cited as an 87-point gap he calls not meaningful

takeaways.technique: Novelty budget as a planning artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Before a project starts, name the one thing that is genuinely novel and review it like a spend line item; if you cannot name it, label the work a learning exercise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Before the bill starts, name the one thing that is novel. If you don't have one, then you can take the median.

takeaways.technique: Open weights are not open inference (10-layer cost gap)
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that between open weights and a token-generating service sit ~10 layers (MLOps, SRE, precision/KV cache, batching, parallelism, utilization) that are structural and cannot be bought cheaply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Open weights are at rage, but open weights are not open inferences.
takeaways.numbers: cites 10 layers between open weight and token generation
